notes:
Summary: Enterprise customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive chat + reranking at scale. Primary ask = contractual throughput guarantee (min tokens/sec) with explicit concurrency caps and a bounded burst policy. Wants clear mapping between reserved GPUs and guaranteed throughput.

Key requirements / quotes: 
- "Need a hard min tokens/sec so our front-end autoscaler can rely on steady token output during peak shopping hours."
- Sustained target: 1,500 tokens/sec minimum per customer shard for 95% of 10-minute windows (customer-proposed metric).
- Concurrency expectations: baseline concurrency cap = 80 concurrent inference sessions; long-term goal 150 concurrency with autoscale.
- Burst policy: allow short bursts to 150 concurrent sessions for up to 5 minutes with proportional rate-limited tokens/sec (graceful degradation), and a cooldown of 15 minutes. Wants documented burst charges.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for 64-token outputs (generation-first-token tail important). Customer will accept higher p99 for >1024 token sequences but wants escalation path.
- Reserved GPU planning: proposed plan = 2 shards x 4 H100 each (8 H100 total) as reserved pool. Redwood should map this to the min tokens/sec guarantee and show calculation assumptions (model type, quant, batch sizing).
- Model preferences: primarily open encoder-decoder variants, fine-tuned Llama-family variants; willing to use Redwood-verified quantized variants if quality checks pass.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high. Willing to commit to annual reserved plan if guarantees (throughput + latency) are iron-clad and credits applied to long-running traffic.
- Security: must support SAML SSO, KMS integration for keys, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, and VPC peering with private endpoints. Data residency: primary NA; EU satellite for EU customers.

POC plan (customer proposed):
- 60-day POC, 2-week benchmarking + warm-up, then 4-week production-like soak where we validate throughput SLA at 99% compliance for min tokens/sec across daily peaks.
- Redwood deliverable: perf profile (tokens/sec per H100 at typical seq len), suggested shard sizing, burst policy language, and incident runbook.

Open negotiation points / AE notes: 
- Legal wants explicit definitions: "sustained" window, token measurement method (decoded tokens vs. input+output), and acceptable maintenance windows.
- Customer asks for concurrency caps tied to user tiers (e.g., premium vs. standard). Need product to confirm per-route concurrency enforcement.
- Pricing ask: include burst buffer credits (prepaid) vs overage billing. Customer prefers capped overage to avoid surprise bills.
- SE action: Priya to provide microbenchmark matrix (seq lengths 32/64/256), mapping of min tokens/sec -> reserved H100 count, and recommended batcher config.
